fullPassage:
Astronaut Yujin's Space Log

Day 1 Back to Space!
After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked successfully. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest artificial space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth!

Day 5 The World with No Gravity
Now I'm getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often confused about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a superhero. Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.

Day 25 Starting the Day
The station orbits Earth once every 90 minutes, and the sun rises and sets every 45 minutes. However, our schedules are set to Greenwich Mean Time on Earth.

My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything floats. Then, I look over the daily schedule sent by the flight control team on Earth. After a meeting with the Earth team at 7:30, I start work.

Every minute of an astronaut's day is planned by the Earth team. My work comprises lots of scientific experiments and maintenance of the station. My favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I film its growth every day. Having green plants in space is a delight!

Day 60 Spacewalk!
Today's mission required a spacewalk, one of the riskiest tasks on the ISS. We had to install the bases for some newly developed solar batteries on the outside of the station.

Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a room connected to the outside of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated gently into space. The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the airlock. We moved along the handrail to the edge of the station. The dark void in front of us seemed endless. Despite the safety cable, panic rose in me. I thought, "If my hand misses the handrail, I will fall into the void." The task seemed to take forever, but I finally managed to install the battery bases. When I turned my head, the bright blue Earth was still there. In the middle of darkness, its beauty was beyond description.

Day 99 One Day Left
I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is alarming and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk. I'll especially miss my basil plants, whose leaves have become a dense forest! All the same, I'll never forget how lucky we are to have that wonderful blue planet as our home.

Day 100 The Descent to Earth
Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.

After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was scorched black. We were falling faster than the speed of sound. Once we got into the atmosphere about eight kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us with a sudden halt and dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky until we hit the ground.

It's hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt terribly heavy, and so did my legs. Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time. The important thing is I'm home. I can smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! I'll remember how magical these things are for the rest of my life.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ lifting → to lift: 'not only to fly but also to lift'에서 상관접속사 not only A but also B 병렬 구조. to fly와 to lift가 병렬.
det.analysis:
✅ ① docked: 과거형 적절. 'we docked successfully' 과거 사건 서술
✅ ② readjusting: 'it's my brain readjusting' 현재분사 적절
❌ ③ lifting → to lift: 'not only to fly but also to lift' 병렬 구조. to fly에 맞춰 to lift 필요 ←정답
✅ ④ were: 'as if each were a floor' 가정법 과거 적절
det.tip: not only A but also B: A와 B는 문법적으로 동일한 형태여야 한다(병렬 구조). to fly → to lift.

det.korean: ② sending → sent: 'the daily schedule sent by the flight control team'에서 과거분사가 필요. 일정이 '보내진' 것(수동).

det.korean: ① hovering → hovered: 이 문장의 주어 'The large blue dome of Earth'에 본동사가 필요. 현재분사 hovering은 본동사가 될 수 없다.
det.analysis:

✅ ③ misses: 조건절(If절)에서 현재시제 적절

det.korean: ③ subsided(가라앉다) → rose(올라오다): 안전 케이블이 있음에도 불구하고 공포가 '가라앉은' 것이 아니라 '올라온' 것.
det.analysis:

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 유진과 동료 스콧은 에어록에서 우주복을 입었다.
유진은 핸드레일 없이 자유롭게 우주 공간을 이동했다.
유진은 배터리 기지대를 설치하는 데 성공했다.
유진은 어둠 속에서 밝고 푸른 지구를 보았다.

det.korean: ② 원문에 'We moved along the handrail to the edge of the station.'이라고 핸드레일을 따라 이동했으므로 '핸드레일 없이 자유롭게'는 사실과 다름.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 'went to an airlock, put on our spacesuits' — 원문 일치
✅ ② '핸드레일 없이 자유롭게'는 원문과 반대. 핸드레일을 따라 이동 ←정답
❌ ③ 'I finally managed to install the battery bases' — 원문 일치
❌ ④ 'the bright blue Earth was still there' — 원문 일치
det.tip: 'along the handrail' = 핸드레일을 따라. 우주유영 시 반드시 잡고 이동해야 한다.

questions.passage: Once we got into the atmosphere about eight kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us with a sudden halt and ①dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky until we hit the ground. It's hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt terribly ②heavily, and so did my legs. Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time. The important thing is I'm ③home. I can smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! I'll remember how ④magical these things are for the rest of my life.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② heavily → heavy: 'My arms felt terribly heavy'에서 felt는 2형식 감각동사이므로 형용사 보어 heavy가 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① dragged: 과거형 동사. 낙하산이 끌고 흔들었다 — 원문 일치
❌ ② heavily → heavy: 'felt + 형용사 보어' 구조. terribly(부사)가 heavy(형용사)를 수식. heavily(부사)는 보어 불가 ←정답
✅ ③ home: 'I'm home' 부사적 용법 적절
✅ ④ magical: 'how magical these things are' 감탄문 구조에서 형용사 적절
det.tip: 감각동사(feel, smell, taste, look, sound) + 형용사 보어. heavily(부사) → heavy(형용사).

questions.passage: Now I'm getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often confused about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a superhero. Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.
questions.stem:
Q: 위 글에서 유진이 하루에 150분 운동하는 이유를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어) (영어로)
A: 무중력이 우주비행사의 근육과 ___ ___를 잃게 하기 때문이다.

det.korean: 무중력이 근육과 bone density(골밀도)를 빠르게 잃게 하므로 하루 150분 운동한다.
det.analysis: ✅ bone density: 'zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I exercise for 150 minutes a day' 원문에서 확인.
det.tip: bone density(골밀도): 무중력 환경에서 감소하는 핵심 건강 지표. That's why가 이유 연결.

questions.passage: After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was scorched black. We were falling faster than the speed of sound.
questions.stem:
Q: 위 글에서 중력이 돌아오면서 시계가 어떻게 느껴졌는지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (3단어) (영어로)
A: My watch felt ___ ___ ___.

det.korean: 시계가 a lot heavier(훨씬 더 무겁게) 느껴졌다. 중력이 돌아오면서 물체가 무겁게 느껴지는 현상.
det.analysis: ✅ a lot heavier: 'My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist' 원문에서 확인.
det.tip: a lot heavier = 훨씬 더 무거운. a lot + 비교급 = 비교급 강조 표현.

questions.passage: Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a room connected to the outside of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated gently into space. The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the airlock. We moved along the handrail to the edge of the station. The dark void in front of us seemed endless. Despite the safety cable, panic rose in me.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 우주유영 중 안전 케이블이 있음에도 유진에게 솟아오른 감정을 나타내는 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 안전 케이블이 있음에도 불구하고(Despite the safety cable) 유진에게 솟아오른 감정은 panic(공포, 극심한 두려움)이다.
det.analysis: ✅ panic: 'Despite the safety cable, panic rose in me.' 원문에서 확인.
det.tip: panic = 극심한 공포/공황. 'rose in me'는 '내 안에서 올라왔다'는 의미.

questions.passage: It's hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt terribly heavy, and so did my legs. Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time. The important thing is I'm home. I can smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! I'll remember how magical these things are for the rest of my life.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 중력 적응 훈련을 철저히 해야 한다.
지구로 돌아온 후 일상적인 것들의 소중함을 깨닫게 된다.

det.korean: ③ 풀냄새, 바람, 비 같은 일상적 요소를 '마법 같다(magical)'고 느끼며 평생 기억하겠다는 내용.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 위험성 경고가 아니라 귀환 후 감상을 서술
❌ ② 훈련 필요성이 아니라 감사함을 표현
✅ ③ '풀냄새, 바람, 비'라는 일상을 magical이라 표현 — 소중함 깨달음 ←정답
❌ ④ 우주가 편리하다는 내용은 없음
det.tip: 요지 = 글쓴이의 핵심 메시지. 'how magical these things are' = 일상의 소중함.

questions.passage: Now I'm getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often confused about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a superhero. Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 무중력 환경이 인체에 미치는 영향과 적응

det.korean: ④ 무중력에서 신체 위치 혼란, 벽을 바닥처럼 사용, 초인적 힘, 근육/골밀도 감소, 운동 등 인체 영향과 적응을 다룸.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 선발 기준은 언급되지 않음
❌ ② 수면 장애 '치료법'이 아니라 무중력 환경 전반의 신체 영향
❌ ③ 정거장 내부 구조가 아니라 무중력이 신체에 미치는 영향
✅ ④ 위치 혼란 + 초인적 힘 + 골밀도 감소 + 운동 = 인체 영향과 적응 ←정답
det.tip: 주제 = 글의 중심 소재. 무중력(zero gravity)의 신체 영향이 반복 서술.

questions.passage: I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is alarming and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk. I'll especially miss my basil plants, whose leaves have become a dense forest! All the same, I'll never forget __________ that wonderful blue planet as our home.

overlay.blank: how lucky we are to have

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오.

"우리가 얼마나 운이 좋은지를 (가지고 있다는 것을)"

[조건] (1) are, have, how, lucky, to, we를 모두 사용
(2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것
(6단어) (영어로)
questions.wa: how lucky we are to have
accept: how lucky we are to have

det.korean: I'll never forget how lucky we are to have that wonderful blue planet as our home — 감탄사절(how+형용사+주어+동사) + to have.
det.analysis:
✅ how lucky we are to have: how+형용사+S+V 감탄사절 구문. to have는 가지고 있다는 것의 to부정사.

→ 본문: I will never forget how lucky we are to have that wonderful blue planet as our home.
→ 구문: forget + 감탄사절(how lucky we are) + to have(~을 가지고 있는)
det.tip: how + 형용사 + S + V = 감탄사절. forget how lucky we are = 우리가 얼마나 운이 좋은지 잊지 않겠다.
